children: TOKYO--Consumer inflation picked up in Japan's capital last month, likely fueling speculation of more interest-rate hikes ahead.

Consumer prices excluding fresh food climbed 2.7% in September from a year earlier, accelerating from a 1.8% rise in August, government data showed Friday. That beat the 2.4% increase expected in a poll of economists by data provider Quick.

While the effects of Tokyo's water bill subsidies faded, food prices remained high as Japanese companies passed along rising shipping and packaging expenses driven by the Middle East conflict. Food prices excluding fresh items rose 3.6% on the year, growing at the same pace as in August.

With Tokyo figures considered a leading indicator of nationwide trends, the uptick is likely to add to expectations that the Bank of Japan will tighten policy in the coming months to combat persistent inflation.

Following the BOJ's decision to raise its policy rate to 1.25% in September, many economists and investors expect the central bank to raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points by the end of the year.

BOJ policymakers, including Gov. Kazuo Ueda, have said the bank has entered a phase where it should pay closer attention to upside risks to prices. Some economists say the bank could move as early as this month if the yen comes under renewed pressure, risking an overshoot of the bank's 2% inflation target.
